title: PDB Molecule Loader (Caffeine Ball-and-Stick Model)
prompt:
Use Three.js to implement a PDB text parser and ball-and-stick molecular viewer for caffeine.

[Three.js Import Method (Must Be Followed Strictly)]
Use the following importmap in <head>, and import through ES Modules in <script type="module">:
<script type="importmap">
{ "imports": {
    "three": "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/build/three.module.js",
    "three/addons/": "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/examples/jsm/"
} }
</script>
<script type="module">
import * as THREE from 'three';
import { OrbitControls } from 'three/addons/controls/OrbitControls.js';
</script>

[PDB Data]
(1) Hard-code a real or approximate caffeine PDB containing ATOM lines as a string constant in the code, and parse it at startup.
(2) Parse ATOM records: atom name, x, y, z, and element (from the element column or inferred from the atom name).

[Rendering]
(3) Ball-and-stick model: render atoms as spheres and color them by element: C gray, H white, O red, N blue, and S yellow (if present).
(4) Bonds: connect atom pairs whose distance is less than or equal to 1.6Å using cylinders.
(5) Bond types: determine single bonds (thin cylinders) and double bonds (two slightly offset, parallel thin cylinders) based on the types of the bonded atoms.

[Interaction]
(6) OrbitControls.
(7) Clicking an atom: display that atom's information in an information panel (a DOM element with id="atomInfo" may be used).
(8) Measurement: after clicking two atoms, display the distance between them (Å); provide a button with id="clearMeasure" to clear the current measurement and selected points (optional but recommended).
(9) Display mode toggle button with id="displayMode": switch among ball-and-stick / space-filling / wireframe (or equivalent English enum values); window.__3D_STATE__.displayMode must be the current mode string.

[State Exposure (Required; Update Every Frame or After Each Interaction)]
window.__3D_STATE__ = {
  atomCount: number,
  bondCount: number,
  selectedAtom: null | { element, name, x, y, z, ... },
  measurementDistance: number,  // 0 when no measurement has been formed
  displayMode: string,
  atoms: Array<{ element: string, x: number, y: number, z: number }>  // For validation; all coordinates must be finite numbers
}

After parsing caffeine, atomCount should be 24 and bondCount should be greater than 20.

Output a single HTML file that can run when opened directly in a browser.
